Scenarios.Scenario: Discovering Copilot/CLI language models and rendering the model picker, cards, and hovers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A cold provider refresh must obtain the existing model catalogue and send its model array across the extension-host boundary before the picker can show it; warm CLI reads use the cached promise. The changed code only copies one numeric field per model and performs an O(1) arithmetic helper during card/hover rendering, with no new await or layout read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch available CLI/Copilot model metadata on a cold catalogue load
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One getAvailableModels call for a cold session cache, shared by all later callers; zero on warm reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same catalogue request and per-model mapping occurred before the diff; the mapped DTO omitted the independent context-window scalar.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold model discovery waits for the existing call; warm picker opens do not. Copying maxContextWindowTokens adds no call or await.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Return provider model metadata from the extension host to the workbench
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing provider response containing N model DTOs per provider refresh; payload grows by at most one number per model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same model array crossed IPC without maxContextWindowTokens.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The provider response is required for model registration, but the diff neither adds a round trip nor changes refresh frequency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of advertised models; each refresh still maps the catalogue once, and each visible card/hover performs one constant-time context-window calculation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: CLI package/auth acquisition is already parallelized with Promise.all, and the available-model promise is shared for the VS Code session. Picker rendering remains synchronous per rendered model; the diff adds no task or concurrent operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CopilotCLIModels caches the in-flight/resolved model fetch for the session and clears it only after failure; workbench language-model metadata remains in the existing local model map. The added scalar does not alter keys, invalidation, negative-cache behavior, or coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed lines only propagate existing metadata and replace an add with a few arithmetic operations; call paths and cache ownership are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact catalogue size and cold network latency vary, but the incremental work is a bounded scalar per already-serialized model and constant-time UI arithmetic.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. There is no new boundary, repeated collection scan, eager heavyweight work, or synchronous layout mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening Copilot cloud-session options and showing model metadata in the session picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a cold options-cache miss, the provider already resolves repository state, CCA state, remote option data, repository items, and local custom-agent files before returning options. The changed line merely copies max_context_window_tokens from each already-fetched model into its option DTO; hover construction remains local synchronous DOM creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch custom agents, Copilot agent models, and partner agents
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: On a cold cache miss, one global model request plus up to two repository-scoped requests, grouped in one parallel batch; zero on an options-cache hit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical remote requests produced model option DTOs without the independent context-window field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing requests gate cold option construction. The diff consumes an additional field from the model response but does not add or move a request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing scan over relevant workspace agent directories on a cold options-cache miss; unaffected by model count and unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same local-agent scan occurred before the metadata propagation change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing scan completes before option groups are returned; the new model scalar does not affect it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Remote model count N and workspace/repository agent-file count; the diff adds one property assignment for each model and does not change file or network cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Custom-agent, global-model, and partner-agent requests run in one existing Promise.allSettled batch. Local filesystem enumeration and repository option handling preserve their existing sequencing; no concurrency is introduced or enlarged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The completed option groups use the existing repository-keyed TTL options cache. Warm calls return cached options, and the new property does not alter the key or invalidation behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed hunk is inside the post-fetch model mapping and introduces no control-flow or boundary change.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Workspace file counts and remote latency vary, but none of those costs changes with this diff; incremental allocation is one optional number on each already-created model DTO.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Cold/warm behavior, batching, and boundary cardinality are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Publishing renderer BYOK models to the local agent host and launching a BYOK-enabled Copilot session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial BYOK availability requires a renderer-local enumeration and one pushed IPC snapshot. Agent-host refresh then reads the registry cache synchronously. Session launch reads the cached models and starts the existing memoized loopback proxy only when models exist; adding independent prompt/output limits only enriches the snapshot and generated session config.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Push the filtered BYOK model snapshot from renderer to agent host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial snapshot and at most one serialized/coalesced publish per debounced model-change burst; one array of N BYOK DTOs, not one call per model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same snapshot schedule and array crossed IPC with total context size but without independent prompt/output limits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial snapshot enables BYOK models; later updates refresh cached model state. The diff adds two optional numbers per model but no extra IPC event.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply provider/model configuration while launching the existing Copilot CLI-backed session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One session-config synthesis per launch and one lazily memoized loopback proxy for all N models; no per-model subprocess or IPC call is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Session launch already synthesized N model entries and configured the same providers/proxy, carrying only total context limits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing session launch consumes the config; two scalar properties enlarge each model config but do not add launch stages or round trips.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of renderer language models scanned M and effective visible BYOK models N after filtering; comparison, snapshot serialization, agent-model mapping, and session-config synthesis remain O(M) or O(N) with two additional scalar fields per BYOK model.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Renderer language-model changes are debounced by 500 ms. AgentHostClientByokLmChannel serializes and coalesces publishes with a Throttler; the registry structurally suppresses identical snapshots. Session launch uses the existing memoized single proxy handle rather than starting one per model.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The bridge registry caches one latest snapshot per connection, selects one serving window, distinguishes not-yet-published from empty, and suppresses unchanged arrays. Added token fields participate in equality so only real limit changes propagate. The loopback proxy handle remains lazily memoized.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: event sources, coalescer, registry cache/equality, and launch call path were directly inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installed provider/model counts vary, but effective snapshot frequency is bounded by debounce, throttling, and equality checks. The incremental payload is linear only in the already-bounded model catalogue.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR preserves coalescing and adds only bounded metadata; actual limit changes appropriately trigger one refreshed snapshot.

Scenarios.Scenario: Updating the chat context-usage gauge after responses, model selection, or configuration changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Response and selection events synchronously look up in-memory model metadata, resolve an in-memory configuration, calculate the denominator, and update existing DOM nodes. The new helper uses constant-time addition/minimum logic and performs no geometry read, network access, IPC, or filesystem operation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected/effective model and one usage record per update event; cost does not scale with conversation history or model catalogue size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Updates remain synchronous on the UI event path with no asynchronous fan-out. Existing event filtering limits configuration-triggered rerenders to the displayed/selected model.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Language-model metadata and model configuration are existing in-memory service lookups. No cache, key, negative state, or invalidation policy is changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the full update and render path shows only property reads, arithmetic, class/text updates, and existing progress rendering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Response event frequency depends on existing model update behavior, but each changed computation is O(1) and adds no layout-forcing operation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed calculation does not introduce measurable repeated work, boundary traffic, retained state, or forced layout.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 34 changed files and all diff pages. Traced catalogue discovery, cloud-session option loading, extension-host and agent-host IPC, BYOK session launch, caches/coalescers, and synchronous picker/context rendering. The PR propagates bounded scalar metadata and performs constant-time calculations without adding expensive boundary calls, increasing call frequency/concurrency, defeating caches, or retaining unbounded state; no findings or regression-fix record are warranted.
